reasoning: Spain top the market as reigning European champions with arguably the deepest squad in the field — an elite Rodri/Pedri midfield, a returning-to-fitness Lamine Yamal and a defense that conceded very little in qualifying — and enter the knockouts unbeaten and topping Group H. Argentina are the strongest counter as defending champions who won all three group games with a positive goal difference and have Messi in scoring form, making a Spain-Argentina title clash the most likely outcome. The main threats are France (perfect group record, GD +8) and an in-form England, though France's leaky defense was exposed in a wild 4-6 loss to England, and both could meet Spain or Argentina before the final. Morocco is the live outsider: they matched Brazil for points in Group C, have shown knockout resilience, and could exploit heat, altitude and travel factors in the North American host venues.
